correctness.rationale: For radial \(u=t^{-a}v(\log t)\), the weighted gradient and Hardy terms reduce exactly to \(\omega_{N-1}\int |av-v'|^N\) and \(\omega_{N-1}a^N\int|v|^N\). A compact plateau cutoff of length \(L\) makes the defect \(O(L^{-1})\) after the linear Taylor term integrates to zero, while the \(X_2^q\) remainder is bounded below by \(cL^{1-q}\). Hence the ratio is \(O(L^{q-2})\to0\) for every \(q<2\). The exponential-optimality consequence then follows from the focal paper’s parameter-independent Young factorization and degree-\(N\) homogeneity. All hypotheses and quantifiers were checked; no finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The focal theorem deliberately leaves exponent optimality unstated for \(\beta>1\) even though its positive embedding covers that regime. The result closes that natural parameter gap and identifies the exact obstruction needed by the source’s own optimality mechanism. The cutoff reduction also gives a reusable structural explanation for why power \(2\) remains the boundary on the upper-weight side; this is not a routine restatement or a tiny numerical improvement.
